body.statement: On every observable law satisfying Conditions 2--3 of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki (2026), the rigid value returned by \(\mathscr A\) equals the PN/PS value obtained from their Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33). The same atlas is defined on additional singular and boundary observable laws not covered by those regular conditions, including design-A support-face strata with rank loss, coincident endpoints, inactive rows, or forced-zero incident coefficients and analogous design-B strata governed by response-level shared-\(Z\) residual forests. On each such law, the full-rigidity theorem returns either a target-rigidity certificate with an exact value or a legal target-changing full-SCM certificate.
body.justification: The theorem verifies published regular formulas and proves that the same structural compiler remains defined on all singular and boundary fibers.
body.gap: The anchor paper does not supply a full-fiber classifier when its regular inversions fail.
body.consumer: Users can retain the published value on regular tables and switch to an exact rigidity or countermodel certificate elsewhere.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p)\) denote the pair in Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33) of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki.  On an observable law satisfying their Conditions 2--3, every compatible member of the present anchor-model fiber satisfies their Condition 1 by the defining response, selection, and proxy factorization.  The cited regular-identification lemma therefore gives
\[
\tau(\vartheta)=R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p)
\qquad\text{for every compatible }\vartheta. \tag{15}
\]
The cited lemma includes the positive-observed-probability condition, so every conditioning operation in (15) is defined.  Hence the full target image is the singleton \(\{R_{\mathrm{SYK}}(p)\}\).  By the full-rigidity theorem, \(\mathscr A\) declares this fiber rigid and returns its unique value, which by (15) is precisely the published Appendix value.

For any other nonempty observable fiber, including a rank-one cell, coincident endpoint, inactive coefficient row, or forced-zero face, the structural equality (6) assigns every design-A cycle point to a local mode and support chart.  In design B, (12) additionally assigns every compatible point to either the zero-residual or active proportional state at each response type and imposes all forest scales, cycle products, and relevance.  Thus these singular and boundary laws are in the domain of the same compiler, without invoking the regular inversions in (15).  The full-rigidity theorem then returns exactly one of two exhaustive alternatives: all one-copy component projections agree at an exact target value, or two component samples lift to legal target-changing SCMs.  This proves the universal boundary-coverage clause as well as regular-domain agreement.
